reviews.lens: code correctness, deterministic replay integrity, and Opik lifecycle auditability

findings.criterion: Proof verifiability for external storage claims
findings.observation: The current proof package now describes the `ReplacingMergeTree` retry semantics honestly, but the specific claim of 26 physical upsert rows versus 13 unique logical spans is still not independently evidenced by any preserved raw query or storage artifact inside the checked proof bundle.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/README.md:41-45 explicitly distinguishes physical storage rows from logical spans; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:123-127 records `remoteUniqueSpanCountBeforeRetry: 13`, `remoteUniqueSpanCountAfterRetry: 13`, `duplicateLogicalSpanGrowth: 0`, and `physicalUpsertRowsAfterRetry: 26`; scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs:124-135 only reasserts those literals; a 2026-09-01 directory scan of docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform found 0 artifact files with names indicating span-table, ClickHouse, query, row-count, or physical-row evidence.
findings.user_impact: Future reviewers can verify that the code uses content-addressed span IDs, but they cannot independently falsify the stronger claim that the remote backing store physically held exactly 26 row versions after retry rather than that number being copied forward into prose and proof JSON.
findings.recommendation: Preserve one raw, task-scoped evidence artifact for the external storage observation itself, such as a query result export or structured count report that names the 13 unique span IDs and the 26 physical row versions, then bind the proof validator to that artifact instead of to hard-coded numeric literals alone.
findings.verification: Add a checked artifact containing the raw storage/query result for the retry run, then require `node scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs` to recompute or cross-check the 13 logical span count and 26 physical row count from that artifact.

strengths: The CLI Opik boundary now enforces an explicit AgentDefinition digest before any side effect: apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:90-105 rejects missing `--agent-definition-digest`, and a real run of `pnpm --filter @talent-signal/eval-runner replay -- --id TS-TRJ-005 --opik --agent-definition-id pursuit-agent-evaluation --agent-definition-version 1.0.0 --artifact-dir <tmp>` exited 1 with `Opik projection requires --agent-definition-digest` while creating no output directory.

Trial identity and source-tree fingerprinting are now part of immutable run identity: apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:114-135 includes `trial-${envelope.trialNumber}` and `trial_number` in Experiment identity; apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:137-169 and 227-269 compute an `evaluation-runtime` source-tree digest and pass it into the Attempt fingerprint; apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:97-136 and 201-219 place that fingerprint in the Attempt content and derive `runId` from the full Attempt digest plus suite digest. Real CLI replay of `TS-TRJ-005` showed trial 1 and trial 2 produced different attempt IDs, attempt digests, and run IDs while preserving the same output digest.

The proof and validator now bind deletion and cleanup claims back to checked artifacts: scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs:165-180 ties proof.deletion IDs to the checked deleted experiment and validates the deletion receipt; scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs:210-217 requires cleanup status `completed` with zero remaining task-owned containers, volumes, and networks; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/projection-ledger-final-v2-r5/opik_evaluation_run_0f6a1ba9a24c2816323059669c23bab4/0003-succeeded-716653b5d033.json:13-17 and the paired deletion receipt at deletion_opik_evaluation_run_0f6a1ba9a24c2816323059669c23bab4_3c7b248032e3.json:3-15 carry the exact localArtifactDigest, external trace ID, experiment ID, experimentItem ID, and deletion reason the proof cites.
missing_evidence: No automated test in the checked test suites covers the CLI-only negative path that `--opik` without `--agent-definition-digest` must fail before any artifact write; that behavior was verified only by a real command in this review.
No preserved artifact in docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform independently records the raw remote storage/query state behind the `physicalUpsertRowsAfterRetry: 26` claim.
open_questions: Do we want the final proof to keep physical storage-row counts at all, or should the proof scope narrow to logical trace/span behavior unless a raw database evidence artifact is intentionally retained?
Should the CLI digest requirement gain a dedicated regression test so `pnpm eval:ci` fails immediately if a future refactor weakens that boundary?

Local authority still leads projection, survives failed remote projection, and remains the retained authoritative surface after scoped deletion: packages/evaluation/src/localJsonReporter.ts:180-257; apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:221-273; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.ts:82-129, 230-285; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:142-206; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/projection-ledger-corrective-v1/opik_evaluation_run_51c04c5795695ba862f9d0e8ee2ecf33/0003-failed-633e7c600464.json:1-20; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/projection-ledger-corrective-v1/opik_evaluation_run_51c04c5795695ba862f9d0e8ee2ecf33/0009-succeeded-6738d0476a1c.json:1-20.

I do not see live executable evidence here for deidentified_governed, private_reference_only, or prohibited_export scenarios against a real Opik destination, only contract and policy enforcement for those classes: apps/eval-runner/src/safeExportPolicy.ts:94-113, 353-410; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:4-24, 130-206.

Scoped deletion is now truthful about retainedSurfaces, but the packet still does not prove any broader vendor-side control beyond trace_projection scope, such as backups, region, or production retention behavior. The PRD explicitly keeps those questions out of the local M3 proof: apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.ts:239-284; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/projection-ledger-final-v2-r5/opik_evaluation_run_0f6a1ba9a24c2816323059669c23bab4/deletion_opik_evaluation_run_0f6a1ba9a24c2816323059669c23bab4_3c7b248032e3.json:1-15; plans/2026-08-31-evaluation-first-opik-agent-platform.md:761-778, 1302-1305.

reviews.lens: boutique recruiter operational fit for evaluation-platform release semantics, workflow evidence requirements, typed review boundaries, and score honesty
strengths: Missing required human-workflow evidence is now attributed only to the workflow capability instead of contaminating decision, scenario, and trajectory. packages/evaluation/src/gates.ts:71-76 maps required evaluator bindings to capability names, packages/evaluation/src/gates.ts:115-147 applies missing evaluators per capability, packages/evaluation/src/evaluation.test.ts:519-549 locks the behavior with a unit test, and the current final artifact docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-final-v2-r5/runs/evaluation_run_0f6a1ba9a24c2816323059669c23bab4/run-artifact.1191c6c3a3d5c401f74f269b62733d2e5b9c4270b504a64384706cd460c9bdc4.json:1 shows decision/scenario/trajectory at pass while workflow alone remains needs_review.

Overall P0 release readiness still stays needs_review when human workflow evidence is absent. evals/v2/suites/p0-release.v1.json:6-8 defines that suite purpose explicitly, docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:142-149 records 12 deterministic-safety passes with 12 release-readiness needs_review results and reasonCode HUMAN_WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED, and node scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs currently returns releaseReadiness needs_review.

The 12 P0 scenarios do not fabricate human gold. evals/v2/README.md:37-40 and 57-69 state that imported annotations remain unreviewed proposals and that the initial bank truthfully remains unreviewed until explicit atomic adjudication exists; evals/v2/suites/p0-release.v1.json:8-78 lists P0 entries with adjudication set to unreviewed; representative scenario docs such as evals/v2/scenarios/ts-trj-005.r1.json:12-15 and 79-79 also remain unreviewed with empty criterionAdjudications; a read-only repository count confirmed p0_count 12, not_unreviewed [], and nonempty_criterionAdjudications [].

Deterministic safety, release readiness, and candidate-value ranking remain explicitly separate. docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/README.md:11-18 and 34-39 say deterministic safety passed while local gates stayed needs_review and that no candidate conversation or candidate scoring claim is present; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:10-15 excludes any claim that deterministic pass equals recruiter approval or release approval; evals/v2/README.md:12-14 and 81-84 say the cases score Talent Signal behavior and recruiter workflow, never a candidate, and that pass is not an aggregate score; evals/v2/review/reviewer-guide.v1.md:3 and 31-33 forbid candidate-worth judgments and prevent model review from owning P0 authority.

Typed boundary discipline is enforced across observation and remote-response contracts. apps/eval-runner/src/contracts.ts:46-62 requires reviewBoundary on every observation, apps/eval-runner/src/reviewBoundary.ts:28-35 and 50-167 type and validate evidence, confirmedState, interpretations, proposedActions, and observedOutcomes, and apps/eval-runner/src/builtinExecutors.ts:406-455 plus 553-596 build and require the same boundary for control-plane and model/integration paths.

The current repository checks pass on the frozen evidence set. pnpm eval:validate reports status pass with scenarioCount 36, p0Count 12, partitions p0 12 / dev 6 / held_out 8 / red_team 10, and contaminationFindingCount 0; pnpm --filter @talent-signal/evaluation test passes 22 of 22 tests including the missing-workflow-capability regression.
missing_evidence: There is still no named recruiter field study or atomic human-gold corpus proving that the workflow reduces real recruiter correction burden in production conditions. The important improvement is that the repository now preserves that absence honestly instead of translating engineering proof into business validation; see docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/README.md:34-39.

reviews.lens: validity, reliability, fairness, and evaluation design

findings.criterion: Release-readiness and any non-informational evaluation claim require named human-gold authority plus delivered calibration evidence, not only deterministic passes or interoperability proof.
findings.observation: The current platform correctly separates construct, profile, attempt, partition, and criterion-level adjudication, and it correctly prevents model judges from owning P0 authority. However, the reviewed P0 release suite still registers all 12 cases as unreviewed, and the final proof still reports release readiness as needs_review because required human-workflow evidence is missing. I did not find a delivered proof artifact showing 60 adjudicated case-criterion calibration decisions for model use either. That means the platform's guardrails are materially stronger, but release-readiness and calibrated model-use claims remain intentionally unproven.
findings.evidence: packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:25-31 defines mutually exclusive p0/dev/held_out/red_team partitions, and 94-105 defines criterion-level adjudication whose scenario summary carries no authority of its own. apps/eval-runner/src/modeDispatch.ts:32-52 rejects SUT replacement by frozen fixtures and requires a live SUT in integration_probe mode; 55-64 rejects incompatible profiles. apps/eval-runner/src/calibration.ts:21-59 and 155-216 require 60 unique case-criterion decisions, confusion metrics, order stability, repeat stability, adjudication rate, and keep gateAuthority false; 271-299 validates pair identity. apps/eval-runner/src/modelReviewer.ts:72-99 returns needs_review when calibration is not eligible and sets gateAuthority false and p0Authority false. packages/evaluation/src/gates.ts:40-44 forbids model P0 authority and 48-62 preserves veto-first authority instead of averaging. evals/v2/suites/p0-release.v1.json:7-128 shows all 12 registered P0 scenarios still have adjudication 'unreviewed' with the empty criterionAdjudicationDigest. docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:9-15 explicitly limits the claim to interoperability and states the two AgentDefinition versions do not claim quality improvement; 142-148 reports p0ScenarioCount 12, deterministicSafetyPassCount 12, releaseReadinessPassCount 0, releaseReadinessNeedsReviewCount 12, reasonCode HUMAN_WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.
findings.user_impact: This design is safe against a false 'green means release-ready' reading, but stakeholders still cannot honestly treat the package as completed human-workflow validation or as proof that a model judge is calibrated for anything beyond informational, non-P0 use.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current needs_review boundary for release readiness until the proof bundle includes named criterion-level human-gold or adjudication records for the required human-workflow criteria. If model judging is intended for any future non-P0 informational surface, publish a versioned calibration artifact with at least 60 unique case-criterion decisions and the measured false-pass, false-fail, abstention, order, repeat, and adjudication-rate outputs.
findings.verification: This finding is resolved only when reviewers can inspect the named human-gold or adjudication records and, if applicable, a versioned calibration artifact directly from the proof package. If those artifacts remain absent, the falsifiable correct state remains releaseReadinessNeedsReviewCount 12 rather than release approval.

strengths: Construct and SUT validity boundaries are now explicit and enforced at runtime: incompatible profiles are rejected, oracle-like fields are blocked from model-visible input, and integration probes must exercise a live system-under-test component.

Partition independence is materially improved: the repository validates 36 scenarios across mutually exclusive p0/dev/held_out/red_team partitions, and node apps/eval-runner/dist/cli.js validate reported contaminationFindingCount 0 on 2026-09-01.

The final proof makes a narrow, defensible claim: docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json limits the two AgentDefinition comparisons to identity and interoperability and explicitly disclaims any model-quality improvement or release-approval claim.
missing_evidence: No named criterion-level human-gold or adjudication artifact for the 12-case P0 human-workflow gate was included in the reviewed proof package.
No versioned calibration artifact demonstrating 60 unique case-criterion decisions and the resulting threshold metrics was included in the reviewed proof package.
open_questions: Where will the authoritative human-gold or adjudication records live in future proof packages so reviewers can verify release-readiness evidence directly rather than inferring only from suite metadata?
Is a calibrated model judge intended to feed any real non-P0 informational surface soon, or is the current calibration framework still purely preparatory?

top_findings.reason: All 12 P0 scenarios truthfully remain unreviewed; no named criterion-level recruiter gold or delivered 60-decision calibration artifact exists.
top_findings.next_step: Collect authorized atomic human adjudications and publish a versioned calibration artifact before any non-informational evaluator or release claim.
top_findings.verification: The proof bundle exposes named criterion-level records, measured calibration outputs, and the P0 workflow gate changes from needs_review only through human-owned authority.

top_findings.reason: Logical retry identity is preserved, but the exact historical claim of 26 physical ClickHouse row versions lacks a retained raw query artifact.
top_findings.next_step: Bind a task-scoped raw query export into the proof validator, or narrow the proof to the preserved 13 logical identities.
top_findings.verification: A future reviewer can recompute both counts from the checked artifact, or the unsupported physical-row count is absent from the claimed proof scope.

agreements: The evaluation contracts, 36-case partitioning, wrong-SUT controls, deterministic local authority, and three execution modes are implemented and verified.
The Opik integration is optional projection only: safe export precedes network I/O, atomic scores preserve authority, and remote state cannot change the local P0 gate.
No specialist issued a safety veto, and evidence-safety plus recruiter-workflow reviewers returned pass.
A 95/100 engineering integration score is not a specialist-score average and is not release approval; release readiness remains needs_review.
No candidate is ranked or assessed, model review has no P0 authority, and absent human evidence is not fabricated.
adjudication.rationale: Jurisdiction resolves the outcome without averaging. Executable checks and the code, safety, and recruiter reviews support engineering integration at 95/100. Selection science owns the release-evidence claim and keeps it at needs_evidence because all 12 P0 cases lack named atomic human adjudication and no real 60-decision calibration packet exists. The code reviewer also preserves a medium proof-verifiability deduction for the unarchived raw physical-row query. These gaps are explicit deductions and next tests, not hidden implementation passes.

next_tests.test: Run an authorized atomic human-gold program across the P0 workflow criteria and a calibration sample.
next_tests.evidence_required: Named reviewer identity, criterion-level evidence locators and decisions, adjudication trail, at least 60 unique case-criterion calibration decisions, and false-pass/false-fail/abstention/order/repeat metrics.
next_tests.pass_condition: Human-owned P0 workflow evidence is complete without scenario-wide authority promotion, and any model reviewer remains informational until every calibration threshold passes.

next_tests.test: Repeat the Opik idempotent retry with raw storage-query capture, or narrow the proof contract to logical read-model behavior.
next_tests.evidence_required: Task-scoped structured query output listing logical span IDs and physical versions, bound by digest into the validator; alternatively a proof revision that makes no physical-row-count claim.
next_tests.pass_condition: The external storage claim is independently falsifiable from checked evidence and the logical span count remains 13 after retry.

next_tests.test: Before any non-synthetic or non-local projection, run governed export, retention, and scoped-deletion probes against the intended destination.
next_tests.evidence_required: Approved authorization scope, deidentified fixtures, pre-network rejection logs, destination retention configuration, and readback/deletion receipts.
next_tests.pass_condition: No purpose-bound evidence escapes the allowlist, retained surfaces match policy, and every tested deletion scope is reported truthfully.
